item.title: 他拆解疯癫、权力与性，却把自己藏起来丨福柯百年
item.description:
▲ 福柯在家中。（IC photo/图）


全文共10706字，阅读大约需要25分钟

  • 2026年10月15日是福柯诞辰100周年。如果福柯像他的同代人哈贝马斯、乔姆斯基那样长寿，他会见到自己的思想几乎成为常识，影响了人文社科很多领域……

  • 福柯很少对外界披露私人生活。

本文首发于南方周末 未经授权 不得转载


文｜南方周末记者 李慕琰 陈荃新

责任编辑｜刘悠翔

从1979年到1984年，法国《世界报》每周会发表一篇欧洲杰出知识分子的访谈，1980年4月的一篇有些特殊，接受采访的主人公坚持匿名，最后的标题就叫《戴面具的哲学家》。

他解释匿名的原因：“这是出于对一个时代的怀念，在那时，尽管我可以是很不出名的，但是我说的话还是有机会被人们听到……署名使阅读变得太轻率。”他希望更直接地向潜在读者说话，“因为不知道我是谁，你们就会更努力地去探究我为什么要说你们读到的那些话；你们就直说吧，它是对的，它是错的。我喜欢它或者不喜欢它。句号”。

1984年6月，福柯去世几天后，这篇访谈的撰稿人正式公开，匿名者正是福柯。

福柯无疑是那个时代耀眼的学术明星。他逝世时才57岁，正值才能的巅峰期，因猝然的早逝和公开的同性恋性取向，公众对他死因的猜测和质疑甚嚣尘上。当时，距离艾滋病报告第一批病例才三年、被命名才两年，人们对此所知甚少，饱含误解与污名。

和他上一代学者萨特等人主动公开的做法相反，福柯很少对外界披露私人生活。他在生前一次采访中解释：“当记者来了解我的工作情况时，我尽可能地向他讲清楚。但是我的个人生活毫无吸引人的地方……也就没有必要把它公开了。”

几年后，迪迪埃·埃里蓬打算为福柯写一本传记，他与福柯生前相识，多次采访他，但一开始就陷入了纠结：为福柯作传似乎不合适，因为福柯本人多次否认作者这个概念，埃里蓬的朋友们、福柯的亲友都提醒他这一点。

而且，研究福柯还存在特殊困难——他是个复杂多变的人物，福柯的朋友、历史学家杜梅齐尔曾形容，“他戴着面具而且经常更换”。埃里蓬决定不去揭示福柯所谓的真面目，“我不认为在连续改头换面的情况下可以找到其个性的真实性”。在1989年出版的第一本《米歇尔·福柯传》里，埃里蓬谨慎调查与收集事实，系统地还原了福柯一生的经历。

然而，在详尽的传记之下，福柯本人的面目与性情却仍是疑团。美国学者詹姆斯·E.米勒认为：“尽管1989年出版了一部较好的福柯传记，第一次确立了有关他生活和职业的主要事实，但这个人物本身却依旧是个谜，让人捉摸不透。”

不论生前身后，这样的评价紧跟福柯，美国人类学家吉尔茨曾说：“他是一个令人无从捉摸的人物。一个非历史的历史学家，一个反人本主义的人文科学家，一个反结构主义的结构主义者。”

对于福柯来说，固定的形象可能会成为枷锁和规训，如同他在《知识考古学》导言里所写：“不要问我是谁，也别要求我一成不变：这是一种身份的伦理；它决定着我们的身份证件。但愿它让我们在写作时获得自由。”

米勒继续追溯福柯的生平，尤其是未被披露的私人生活部分，尽管他后来出版的《福柯的生死爱欲》受到争议，但显然希望让福柯的面孔变得清晰一些：“朋友们描绘说，这个人极其复杂：灵敏过人，善于自制，沉默寡言时令人尴尬，大笑起来则声震屋瓦——他的笑有时很刻薄，常常是讥讽，富有传奇色彩。”

尽管对自己的生活保持神秘，但福柯同时又一直坦荡承认，他的思想和理论全都建立在他的经验和周围的人发生的事情之上，“我每一次做理论工作，都是从我自己的经验片段出发，永远和我亲眼所见的周遭进程息息相关。正是因为我看见制度、人际关系当中那些裂痕、沉闷的震荡、失灵，我才着手写作，可以说，是某种自传的碎片”，“我的每一本书，都是我个人历史的一部分。出于这样那样的原因，我亲身经历或者感受过这些事”。

其中的自相矛盾，学者高宣扬称之为“不协调”——福柯晚年主张“不必把自己说出来”、把自我交给他人裁判，但他自己一生极不透明，连病因都没有公开确认。“但这个不协调不是瑕疵。他的生活和他的理论在这点上是一致的：拒绝交出自己的秘密，同时主张自己的经验与工作不可分；前者是不招供，后者是不分裂。两者合起来，才是他那个‘自我’的形状——不是被发现的实质，也不是被说出来供人裁断的真相，而是被活出来的实践。”

“他留给人的，是一个充满张力、无法被简单定格的人格形象。”高宣扬对南方周末记者说。

福柯身上具有一种令人怀念的特质，或许是上世纪知识分子才有的秉性：他从来不是象牙塔里的空想家，而是一生都身体力行地践行着自己的思想。

2026年10月15日是福柯诞辰100周年。如果福柯像他的同代人哈贝马斯、乔姆斯基那样长寿，他会见到自己的思想几乎成为常识，影响了人文社科很多领域，在新世纪一再发挥着惊人的解释力。

他对疯癫、理性与精神病历史的考察，成了精神医学与治疗实践绕不过去的前提；他提出的规训权力与全景敞视，至今仍是分析疫情、算法治理、人工智能等当代议题的重要视角；他对性史、性话语的研究，为酷儿理论与身份政治讨论提供了思想资源。

清华大学教授汪民安认为，“如果人们要找一个西方的观念战争和文化战争起源的话，福柯或许是一个隐秘的中心，他是改变今天大学观念最核心的思想人物之一”。

哈贝马斯和福柯只有过一次短暂会面，福柯邀请哈贝马斯在美国伯克利参加一场围绕康德《什么是启蒙？》的学术讨论，这场原定于1984年秋天的讨论最终因福柯离世而取消。哈贝马斯撰文悼念福柯，表达赞赏的同时继续表达了对他观点的保留意见。

他写道：“在与我同代的致力于诊断时代的人之中，福柯对时代精神产生了最为持久的影响，这尤其要归功于他的真诚，他以这种真诚坚持着那些意味深长的矛盾。只有复杂的思想才会产生具有启示意义的矛盾。”

1

米歇尔

“不断地划分正常人和非正常人，使所有人都纳入这种划分。”

福柯全名本来是保罗-米歇尔·福柯，1926年，他出生于法国西部城市普瓦捷的一个医生世家。这个殷实家族从父辈到子辈都给男孩起名保罗，福柯的母亲不愿完全屈从传统，坚持给她的大儿子加上了第二个名字：米歇尔。

长大后，福柯把自己的名字简化为米歇尔·福柯，一种说法是为了与父亲划清界限。福柯与父亲关系不佳，但外界很少探知到具体原因，就像其他方面一样，他对童年时代同样保持缄默，很少在著述中提及。

据另一位传记作者戴维·梅西所写，福柯早在10岁就宣布他不会遵循家庭传统成为医生，当时他想当历史老师。他和父亲的关系因此恶化。福柯的父亲是远近闻名的外科医生，他的祖父、外祖父、弟弟也都如此。

梅西认为，福柯和父亲有显著的差异，但也在某些方面相同。福柯经常把自己描述为诊断专家，把他的著述说成对当下的诊断，而不是永恒真理的载体。一如父亲在人体上做手术，他将手术刀换成了笔。

回顾福柯的人生选择，复旦大学哲学学院教授莫伟民认为，“福柯在专业取舍、情感生活、学术志业上，既抵抗，又选择，这些体验对他的主体理论产生了重要影响”。

福柯家乡普瓦捷的戴高乐广场。（IC photo/图）

福柯的青年时期充满二战的阴影，纳粹的恐怖统治、难民、轰炸都给他留下动荡的记忆，他为数不多谈及早期经历时说：“我相信我这一代的男孩和女孩的童年都是由这些重大历史事件所造就的。战争的威胁充斥我们的生存天地和空间。这些事件给世界带来的影响远远超过了对家庭生活的影响，它构成了我们记忆的质料。我们的个人生活受到了严重的威胁，这或许就是我迷恋历史，迷恋个人体验和我们所亲身经历的事件之间的关系的原因。我想这也是我的理论欲求的出发点。”

至于学业，福柯并非一帆风顺的天才，他极其刻苦地学习，想考巴黎高等师范学院，却在第一次会考中落榜了。1945年秋天，福柯独自搬到巴黎入读预科班，继续备考，其间对哲学产生兴趣。第二年他终于考上了高师。

然而，接下来的高师生涯却是一段痛不欲生的经历。他难以忍受集体生活，孤独、古怪，经常与人争吵，嘲弄他讨厌的同学，给别人起绰号，显得狂妄好辩。他多次企图自杀未遂，也曾伤人和自伤，被视为半疯。

身边的人普遍认为，他的抑郁与性取向带来的压力有关。那个年代，同性恋者在法国处境悲惨，常被视作耻辱，只能秘密活动。

“这些内在的痛苦经验不可能不成为他的思想起源。”汪民安对南方周末记者说，“这也是为什么福柯著作中的主角大都是各种各样的边缘人群，即他笔下的所谓‘不正常的人’，或者主流社会目光中的声名狼藉者。这些人也总是跟疯癫、监狱、性和惩罚密切相关。他努力探讨他们遭受排斥、隔离、驱逐和囚禁的历史原因。他试图为各种各样的受排斥的边缘人群发声，因为他自己多多少少就是其中一员，感同身受。”

入学两年后，父亲带他来到圣-安娜医院求助一位精神病权威，那是法国最大的精神治疗机构。毕业那年，他在好友阿尔都塞的影响下加入了共产党，三年后退出，考了两次才通过法国的大学和中学哲学教师资格考试。

学术生涯早期，福柯密切关注心理学，除了哲学学位之外，他还攻读了心理学学位，当过心理学助教，以实习医生的身份进入圣-安娜医院的脑电波实验室工作。那时的福柯对心理学技术和实验很是热衷，高师的很多同学接受过他各种各样的测试。

很多年后，当别人问起这段经历，福柯否认圣-安娜医院留下了坏印象，恰恰相反，正因为那是一间条件优越的大医院，更迫使他思考自己面对精神治疗感受到的不适，并非源于医院的欠缺，而是整个现代文明对正常与疯癫的定义。

直到1960年他写完以此为主题的近千页博士论文《癫狂与非理性：古典时代疯狂史》（后来出版英译本《疯癫与文明》）之前，福柯先后在瑞典、波兰、德国汉堡工作，担任当地大学法国文化中心的主任，他用大量时间组织文化交流活动，热衷社交往来。梅西记录了一个插曲，在瑞典乌普萨拉，福柯买下一辆价格不菲的二手捷豹跑车，他和法国朋友们经常饮酒作乐，因吵闹的派对变得声名狼藉。

在海外流浪了几年后，法国克莱蒙-费朗大学向福柯抛出了第一个正式的大学教职，让他终于回归法国学术界。他拿到了博士学位，但《疯狂史》被视为一篇稀奇古怪的论文，不遵循学术传统，也很少参考二手资料。他满心希望论文能由大名鼎鼎的伽利玛出版社出版——它出版了知名学者萨特、梅洛-庞蒂的许多著述，但遭到拒绝，只能转由其他出版社。

正式出版后，销量并不理想，福柯多次抱怨这本书问世时遭到的冷遇，“哲学圈子和政治社会对此却不屑一顾。没有任何一本杂志对此表示过关注……”

事实上，福柯的研究已逐渐在学术界引起关注，整个1960年代，他开始大量发表著述。声名将在更晚的时候到来，而早期生活中的边缘经验，构筑了他的哲学起点。

“福柯承认自己写的每一部书都是或至少部分是某种直接被主流社会界定、排斥和规训的个人边缘体验的产物。福柯思想始于自己的个人体验，而非抽象的理论前提。”莫伟民对南方周末记者说。

2

学术明星

“不要问我是谁，也别要求我一成不变。”

1966年，《词与物》出版了，这是福柯最晦涩的一本书，他梳理了16世纪以来的西方知识史，认为每一个历史时期都存在一种隐秘的深层知识结构，决定了那个时代什么知识能被建立、什么思想能被表达，他称之为“知识型”。

因此，“人”这个概念并非古已有之，而是1800年前后伴随现代人文科学兴起而被发明出来的晚近产物。在全书结尾，他提出了震惊世界的预言——“人之死”，“恰似一张画在沙滩上的面孔即将被上涨的潮水抹去”。

莫伟民翻译了《词与物》的中文版，他解读，福柯的“人之生死”定位在19世纪，是指当时人们期望使人成为认识的对象，以使人能成为他自己的自由和他自己的存在的主体。但实际上，福柯断定人们在当时从未发现这个著名的人、人性、人的本质，而只是发现了无意识、结构。“福柯强调人在哲学中消失了，不是作为知识对象的人，而是作为自由和存在主体的人消失了。”

由于内容专业艰深、篇幅冗长，福柯预计这本书能有一两千读者就不错了。谁知甫一出版，初印的数千册就在短短一周内售罄，随后屡次加印，迅速成为巴黎大众媒体和文化阶层人人热议的畅销书，甚至被人们带到沙滩和咖啡馆里阅读，成为当时最瞩目的文化现象。

《词与物》获得了惊人的成功，也让福柯陷入了长久的论战。他的观点冲击了当时在法国大行其道的存在主义潮流，萨特等学者强调人的自由和主体的责任，批评福柯抹杀了历史变迁与人的能动性。福柯在一次电台采访中讥讽：“萨特是有着重要的书要写的人，他要写文学、哲学和政治作品，以致没有时间读我的书。他没有读过我的书，因此，他所讲的不能让我信服。”

相较于《词与物》在法国知识界的巅峰地位，这本书在中国远不如福柯的其他观点和著作有影响力。汪民安分析，人之死的观点是高度理论性和思辨性的，它引发的是知识界内部的哲学论战，对普通读者而言并不具有切身经验，“相形之下，权力、规训、生命政治，人们在生活实践中都能有具身性的感受和体会：谁没有受到过学校的规训？谁没有被各种各样的权力撞击过呢？”

值得注意的是，随着人工智能、大数据和生物基因工程等为代表的科技革命飞速发展，福柯的“人之死”随着这些后人类讨论的展开再次引起关注。“人们一开始听到这声音不明就里，但现在发现它是一个古早的预言。或许每一个概念真的都有它自身的特殊命运。”汪民安说。

成功带来兴奋之余，福柯冷静看待这部给他带来声誉的书，他认定这是他写过的最不好的一本书，甚至一度拒绝再版。

在一次采访中，福柯谈到自己的走红，“这其实是挺烦人的”“大吃一惊，毫无准备”“看来人们对这些著作所要求的不是传统意义上的价值，而是对我们社会深思熟虑、目光长远的看法”。

汪民安认为福柯的成名绝不是单本书带来的偶然，“他的每一本著作都激发了无数的讨论”。福柯生活的20世纪后半叶，大众媒体日渐发达，“他经常接受电视、广播和报刊的采访，他希望将自己的声音放大。那时法国的读书媒体都很严肃，很重视知识分子的思想辩论，读者和观众也基本上是知识分子和青年学生。在媒体上出现的知识分子，都经过了某种不成文的基于多数共识的挑选，所以一般来说保持了基本的智识水准”。

与学术同仁的论战也把福柯一次次推向更大的公共舞台。德里达在一次讲座上批评《疯癫与文明》对笛卡尔的解读，时隔九年后，福柯在这本书再版时写长文回击，措辞尖锐，两人决裂近十年。

他与乔姆斯基的电视辩论，让他在英语世界广为流传，英美学界开始系统引介他的理论。

论战也带来一些副作用，福柯为此和不少朋友决裂，埃里蓬写道：“福柯一旦被触怒，就不会轻易平息下来。在福柯身上存在着‘古代睿智’，这是真的，但他身上还存在着希腊伟大悲剧才具有的那种激情和愤怒的力量。这也是他一生永远不变的特性之一：福柯经常同亲近的人闹翻……有许多名字在福柯面前是绝不能提起的。”

还有一件事更能激起福柯的热情：参与政治行动。他关注权力关系，一生都致力于将自己的理念付诸实践，以此来审视社会政治现实。

1968年，福柯亲身经历、支持和参加了突尼斯学生抗议运动。1971年，他发起创立监狱信息小组（GIP），调查监狱生存状况、推动囚犯发声。1972年，与萨特搁置思想分歧，共同参与抗议移民遇害的反对种族主义行动。1975年，声援遭到佛朗哥军事法庭审判的西班牙反独裁者。1978年，作为特派记者两次赴伊朗，撰文观察反抗巴列维独裁的民众运动。1979年，为救助越南船民，与萨特、阿隆一起召开记者招待会。1981年，与布尔迪厄一起为波兰团结工会奔走呼号。

1972年，福柯与萨特在法国巴黎的雷诺工厂入口前举行示威活动，抗议工人活动家皮埃尔·奥弗涅遇刺事件。（视觉中国/图）

在莫伟民看来，“显然，福柯的政治行动与政治思想就是相辅相成的关系：政治理念指导其政治行动，政治实践修正其政治理论”。

1970年，福柯当选法兰西学院的思想体系史讲座教授，进入这座法国学术圣殿，为他的活动提供了更可靠的支撑。福柯善于演讲，每一次讲座都座无虚席，这一职位持续至他去世。

1980年代，高宣扬在巴黎读博期间，经常去法兰西学院听福柯的讲座，授课的种种细节至今历历在目。听众挤满讲厅，连讲台上都围满了人，学院又在主讲厅之外设立了几个分场，供更多人听课。

“福柯像一个强大吸铁磁那样，吸引厅内外听众，而他自己，在台灯光影之下，一边翻书，一边即席阐发、批判，动作与姿态自成风格；口中每一句话都饱含力量，令所有听众笼罩在严肃、沉静而紧绷的氛围里……他就在众人面前现场思考，坦然呈现当下思考的卡顿、改口与迷途，又展现迂回、突围和急转弯的智慧。音量不大，但信息密度极高，吐字清晰，语速偏快，流畅间夹杂一丝普瓦捷地区口音带来的沙哑。他那当众展露困惑和突围而出的能力，甚至比他最终得出的结论更令人沉醉。与其说他是与人交流，不如说他在搭建思想战场，开辟对话场域。听了一次他的讲演，就迫使你决心再追听下一次。”

高宣扬与莫伟民等学者合写的一篇文章中感叹，福柯的运思方式像极了尼采，但两人的命运迥异，尼采至死都是“异端”，而福柯却在44岁那年堂而皇之地走进了作为西方学术体制最高象征的法兰西学院，成了“主流中的主流”。“造化弄人竟至如此，为之一叹。”

3

极限体验者

“一个人的生命，难道不可以成为一件艺术品吗？”

1983年，一位加拿大记者采访福柯，描述了他的生活：他经常穿着朴素的白裤子、白T恤、黑皮夹克，巴黎的公寓刷成了纯白色，挂着一些黑色雕饰，因为纯黑和纯白“显得直截了当、充满力量”。

他形容福柯的生活“有一种僧侣式的严峻格调”，“看上去不像精致复杂的法国人，他们总想把生活搞成艺术”。

这是福柯接受的采访中罕见聊到个人生活的一次，他甚至袒露自己在体验快乐方面有严重的困难，他希望有过量的快乐，不惜为它死去，对他来说，纯粹的快乐和死亡联系在一起。有一次他在街上走路被汽车撞了，有几秒钟以为自己正在死去，竟然感到了非常强烈的快乐，“这是我迄今为止回忆中最美妙的情景”。

当地时间1981年12月16日，法国巴黎，福柯在一间演播室参与电台广播讲话。（视觉中国/图）

从1970年代中后期起，福柯频繁访问美国讲学，尤其迷恋加利福尼亚和纽约，他喜欢美国西部温和的气候，以及对性少数者更包容的环境，甚至一度考虑离开法国去美国教书。福柯频繁出入湾区的同性恋社区和公共浴室，将其视为一种探索全新生活方式的试验场。

那时福柯在生活和思想上正在发生一系列转向。此前，他已经通过包括《规训与惩罚》在内的多本著作，考察了现代欧洲的主体是如何通过规训权力被塑造而成的，那么，工厂、医院、学校等现代体制出现以前，人的主体是怎么被塑造的呢？他将目光转向古代，包括古希腊、罗马和中世纪，也为了回应一个更直接的问题：人可以如何摆脱规训权力？

“到了晚年，他讨论的最重要的问题是，如果这些东西都是被塑造的、被历史所建构的，那我们为什么还要再去对抗呢？我的对抗是真诚的吗？”上海师范大学教授姚云帆向南方周末记者解读，“作为批判者的福柯很尴尬，那他说，我们唯一能做的事情，就是控制自己的生活方式。”

他已经开启了庞大的《性经验史》写作计划，讨论古希腊人如何通过快感的享用和关切自我来管理自己的生活。他提出“自我技术”（technologies of the self）的概念，也被翻译为自身的技术，主张将自我当作一件艺术品去主动塑造，实现主体的自我构建。

美国学者米勒用福柯曾提出的“极限体验”概念，把他的思想与私人身体经验串联在一起，包括早年的自杀冲动、服用致幻剂的试验、晚年在旧金山社群的活动，甚至最后的死亡都当作追求极限体验的表现。

由此写成的《福柯的生死爱欲》在福柯的亲友和法国学界中引起了不满，他们反对将福柯的学术思想等同于私人情欲实践。

这样大胆的解读或许难掩猎奇和猜度的色彩，但可以肯定的是，福柯生前的确致力于将学术上的思考应用于生活的改造，他说，“我像条狗那样工作了一生，我不关心我所做的工作在学术上的位置，因为我的问题在于对自身的改造”。当人们问，为什么他几年前的一个说法如今变了，他会回答，“你想我干了这么多年，难道就是为了说些一成不变的话吗？”

“通过自己的知识，达到对自我的改造，这就有点像审美经验所起的作用了。一个画家，如果不因为自己的作品而发生变化，那他为什么要工作呢？”福柯说。

从1983年夏天起，持续低烧、头痛、咳喘不断袭来，福柯的健康状况持续衰退。当时艾滋病的检测和治疗还不成熟，医生只能对症处理感染。对于福柯是否知道自己患上了艾滋病，传记作者们说法不一，福柯曾向友人倾诉过怀疑，但没有证据表明他生前得到过确定的诊断。

最后几个月，他在法兰西学院讲授了最后一门课《说真话的勇气》。他反对基督教忏悔式独白，个体被要求交出内心最私密的欲望与秘密，通过坦白和诉说完成自我审查与驯服。相反，福柯推崇古希腊的“直言”（parrhesia），说真话不只是陈述事实，而是在明知要承担风险，甚至危及自身的前提下，主动选择道出真理，这是一种关乎自我塑造的伦理修行。

1984年6月25日，福柯因艾滋病引发的败血症、脑脓肿离世。起初，医院与家属出于保护，并未公开他死于艾滋病，顿时猜测和谣言四起。福柯的长期伴侣丹尼尔·德菲以纪念他为名，创立了法国首个抗艾组织AIDES。几年后，德菲主动对外承认，福柯的死因是艾滋病并发症。

他的死亡掀起一场缠绕着隐私、羞耻与知识分子伦理的漫长争论。法国哲学家让-保罗·阿隆（Jean-Paul Aron）确诊艾滋病后发文，指责福柯当年出于羞耻而选择沉默，没能践行说真话的责任。

姚云帆认为，福柯的选择和他的思想主张并不矛盾，他对于自己所相信的生活方式，没有迟疑、没有后悔，这一点难能可贵，“保持沉默本身就是福柯的性格，因为他不觉得自己应该说出什么，相反他觉得他本身就是莫测的，只要他承认代价就可以”。

在莫伟民的理解里，说真话不是简单地说出一切，而是“有勇气说出自己相信的真理/真相”。福柯并没有违背说真话的原则，“福柯心中有信仰，才会体验激情，经历受难，抒情生死。”。

4

世纪思想家

“看来人们对这些著作所要求的不是传统意义上的价值，而是对我们社会深思熟虑、目光长远的看法。”

福柯的声望在他死后继续上升。米勒引用一位专家的话说，“现在他在学术界拥有一种无人可以匹敌的地位，17世纪以来的西方文明演进的许多关键的方面，都必须按照他的看法来加以解释”。

德菲与人合作整理了福柯散落在各处的访谈、短文、政论，推出四卷本文集，他在法兰西学院的课程录音也陆续被整理成书。按照福柯的遗嘱，未经定稿的手稿原则上不应出版，搁置多年的《性经验史》第四卷，2018年才在争议中面世。

2018年，法国巴黎，福柯的肖像出现在当地报刊上。（IC photo/图）

福柯在中国的影响和西方社会经历了时差。汪民安印象里，福柯的名字最早出现在中国的报刊上，是《国外社会科学》1984年刊登了一则报道他去世的简短消息。1980年代末至1990年代初，福柯的作品开始在国内出版，对他的关注和研究变得越来越多。

汪民安记得一则逸事，福柯的《性史》（后来的中译本采用《性经验史》）在书店里经常被摆在医学和健康的分类柜台，很多年轻人抱着猎奇或科普目的把它买回家，读起来才发现内容晦涩，不知所云。这本书甚至经常出现在中国大中城市的图书地摊上。

北京大学社会学博士曹金羽梳理了福柯在中国的传播过程，“现在活跃的福柯研究者都会提到初读福柯时的震惊和刺激，这几乎是每一个福柯读者初读其作品的体验”。

1993年，莫伟民提交答辩了他的博士论文《主体的命运——福柯哲学思想研究》。他对南方周末记者说：“福柯思想的广度、深度和力度，是20世纪西方思想家无人能及的。”1996年起，北大哲学系的李猛牵头，组织起活跃在北大校园的学术团体“福柯小组”，一起研读、讨论、翻译了上百万字的《福柯文选》。

2000年之后，国内学者展开了对福柯的系统性研究。如今福柯在中国几乎无处不在，各个学科都有大量研究者和爱好者，学者张一兵称，围绕着福柯俨然已经形成了“一个学术劳动密集型产业”。

姚云帆记得，1980年代福柯刚被介绍进来的时候，中国正热烈讨论启蒙理性，福柯的贡献是对理性的质疑，对于中国思想界来说有一定的距离。如今“福柯变成了一个很亲切的思想家，变得非常常识性”。但是，他持续追踪福柯的遗稿，每当读到福柯新的论述，会发现他依然很陌生，总是处于变化之中。

南京信息工程大学教授杜玉生研究了福柯的晚期思想，发现当今有影响力的很多哲学家身上，都能找到福柯的影子。他向南方周末记者举例，德国哲学家韩炳哲的“倦怠社会”，明显结合了福柯的生命政治理论，分析现今社会的绩效主义、自我优化等问题，都能从福柯那里得到启发。

汪民安攻读博士期间把主要精力都放在了福柯身上，读完了他所有重要著作。那些书并不好读，最纠缠他的就是《词与物》，有几个月，他白天晚上都在看，日思夜想都是这本书，如同噩梦缠身。

在福柯不可替代的价值之中，如果非要选出最重要的一个，汪民安认为，就是他的别样思考，“福柯几乎在所有方面都不人云亦云。他总是在很多人思考过的地方提出自己全新的洞见”。

高宣扬初到法国时第一次阅读《词与物》，只觉得读不懂。法国哲学家贾克·董特和福柯曾师出同门，在福柯家乡的普瓦捷大学任教，经常对高宣扬讲述他所看到的福柯。福柯的好友德勒兹也曾与他三次面对面交谈，谈起1968年他们共同参加学生运动。

高宣扬研究了福柯多年，发现“越到后来，他所说的一切，却变成内在于我自己的‘功课’，是属于我自己必须面对和时时验证的一种生活实践。问题不在于从字面上和理论上读懂，因为越钻研和体验他提出的问题，越觉得这些问题本来是属于我的，更确切地说，是我活在这个世界上必须时时面对和解决的生存问题，即是我自己如何做自己和做人的事情”。

他提醒，不要把福柯思想当作知识或工具，福柯从不提供任何正统意义上的真理、方法或锦囊妙计，而是要作为学会自我反思和自我启蒙的参照。

如今86岁的高宣扬历经六十多年哲学生涯，发现哲学不只是一种知识，也不仅仅是大学里的一门专业，它是生命本身的一部分，“在我的一生中，哲学思想的产生与变化，始终跟着我内在的意识、感受、意志、情感和体验一起变动”。当然，这也是福柯的哲学。

（参考资料：迪迪埃·埃里蓬《米歇尔·福柯传》，戴维·梅西《福柯传》，詹姆斯·E.米勒《福柯的生死爱欲》，加里·古廷《福柯》，保罗·韦纳《福柯其思其人》，迪迪埃·埃里蓬《米歇尔·福柯与他的同时代人》，汪民安《福柯的界线》，汪民安、陈永国《福柯的面孔》，高宣扬《福柯的生存美学》，莫伟民《主体的命运——福柯哲学思想研究》，米歇尔·福柯《疯癫与文明》《词与物》《规训与惩罚》《知识考古学》《性经验史》《福柯读本》《权力的眼睛：福柯访谈录》《言说始于死后》）

其他人都在看

item.title: 宝藏敦煌，世无其二
item.description:
公元366年，一个叫乐僔的僧人，独自行走在河西走廊的大漠里。


夕阳将沙丘染成赤金色，他抬起头，忽然看见三危山上金光万道，恍如千佛显灵。


他当即停下脚步，就地开凿了第一个石窟。


没有人知道，这一铲下去，会在这片黄沙之中凿出一座绵延1600多年、举世无双的艺术圣殿。


这就是莫高窟的开始。


此后1650年，无数工匠、僧侣、画师，前赴后继地在这里留下一笔一画。


北凉、北魏、西魏、隋、唐、五代、宋、西夏、元……十六个朝代，潮涨潮落，兴衰更迭。


唯有莫高窟的洞窟，一个接一个地被凿开，一幅接一幅的壁画在黑暗中沉睡，等待着被看见的那一天。


很多人以为，敦煌不过是几面墙上的古画。


直到你真正去了解它，才会明白，这个判断小看了敦煌一万倍。


莫高窟现存735个洞窟，壁画总面积45000余平方米


——如果将所有壁画首尾相连铺展开来，长度超过25公里，堪称人类历史上规模最大的画廊。


其中彩塑2415身，飞天造像4000余身。



而这一切，只是视觉上的冰山一角。


敦煌是丝绸之路的咽喉要道，是中国、印度、希腊、波斯四大文明在地球上唯一的真实交汇点。


它的壁画不只描绘神佛，还记录着一千年前普通人的婚丧嫁娶、农耕宴饮、商旅往来；



它的文献不只有经史子集，还有古人写的离婚协议书、私人账本、医药处方、占星记录；


藏经洞出土的5万余件文物里，有目前世界上已知最早的印刷品，有比欧洲早600年的星图，有迄今发现最完整的中国古代历书……


樊锦诗说，藏经洞出土文献"方面异常广泛，内容无限丰富"，是古代社会文化的原始记录。


历史学家看了，两眼放光。


但就是这样的地方，曾经差点被人彻底搬空。


1900年6月22日，一个叫王圆箓的道士，正在清理莫高窟第16窟积存了数百年的流沙。


他的墓志后来这样记载那个时刻：


"沙出壁裂一孔，仿佛有光，破壁，则有小洞，豁然开朗，内藏唐经万卷，古物多名，见者多为奇观，闻者传为神物。"


这是藏经洞的发现——震惊世界的一次意外。

item.title: Guns, F-bombs, fortune cookies. What do wild campaign ads actually say?
item.description:
Jennifer Balkcom, a Republican running for Congress in western North Carolina, introduced herself to voters by informing them that her single mom once shot a home intruder.

"You break into my house, you're going to get shot," Balkcom's mother says in her twangy mountain accent in a campaign ad posted Sept. 29 on YouTube, which already boasts over 800,000 views.

The camera then pans to Balkcom, a 48-year-old state representative, whose mom says she would bring her family's mountain toughness from their house to the House of Representatives as both women hold white coffee cups at a wooden dining room table.

The commercial is airing in one of the nation's most competitive congressional races and illustrates the metamorphosis of how campaign ads are produced and consumed during this midterm cycle.

Advertisements must be attention grabbing as both parties fight for visibility ahead of Election Day on Nov. 3, political experts, including Travis Ridout, a professor of government and public policy at Washington State University, say.

Can you sue over targeted ads? 'Blockbuster' Supreme Court case to decide

"I think just the capacity to target nowadays and tailor those messages to specific audiences means it's less (of) the standard generic ad that we're trying to appeal to all voters with," Ridout told USA TODAY.

Senator mired in controversy after skipping out on $700 cookie bill

Political spending during the 2025-26 election season has already surpassed $10 billion, exceeding the total ad spending in both the 2019-2020 and 2021-2022 election cycles, according to AdImpact Politics, an ad intelligence firm. AdImpact estimates that this year will mark the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history with upward to $11.6 billion in spending.

But it's not just the sheer size of the ad buys that stand out.

Candidates across the U.S. have used everything from F-bombs to fortune cookies to help boost their own prospects. Wisconsin state Rep. Steve Doyle even held a pet alpaca: "Please, don't fall for emotional appeals. Oh, and this is my baby alpaca, Pasta. She hopes you'll vote for me!" he joked.

Meanwhile, former President Barack Obama cut ads to support a slate of Democratic candidates while some Republicans are using their own spots to seek distance from President Donald Trump, who faces sinking approval ratings.

Viral F-bombs help flip fates in Illinois

In 2024, Cameron Shelton, a political science professor at Claremont McKenna College in California, found in his research that campaign ads confirm previously held biases.

"They're usually just sort of, 'How can I activate latent beliefs that somebody already has with very, very simple language and simple images?'" Shelton told USA TODAY.

Illinois Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton was struggling to break out from second place in February in an expensive, bitter Democratic primary to succeed Sen. Dick Durbin, the No. 2 to Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer.

Advisor Kaitlin Fahey, the CEO at Chicago-based Magnify Strategies political consulting firm, said Stratton had "one shot" to set herself apart from her opponents, Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly.

The Senate races in reliably blue states like Illinois and nearby Minnesota may be sleepier than contests in Michigan or Texas, but the Democratic primaries were no less cutthroat.

Krishnamoorthi touted a massive war chest, including financial support from cryptocurrency PACs, while Kelly, a fellow Black woman, wielded the endorsement of the influential Congressional Black Caucus.

Then Stratton's "f Trump" ad went viral on X and helped her break out of the congested race.

Her Black dad couldn't go to Capitol. She could be a US senator

Trump's Midway Blitz immigration enforcement operations in Chicago had left a sour taste in the mouths of many Democratic primary voters – so Stratton's campaign released the profanity-laced spot in which several voters say "f--- Trump, vote Julianna" directly to the camera.

"They said it, not me," Stratton then quips, before pledging to stand up to the president.

The 30-second video ends with one last "f--- Trump" from Illinois Sen. Tammy Duckworth, and a final "vote Julianna" by Gov. JB Pritzker.

The Stratton apparatus knew the profanity-laced ad would make waves, and ruffle feathers, but it was ultimately successful, Fahey said.

"We also wanted to raise money off of it. We wanted to earn media attention," Fahey said of the viral video.

The ad garnered over 1.6 million all-time views on X. Fahey said her team also wanted the ad to shine more light on the safely blue race but noted that the campaign used other vehicles to discuss Stratton's core policy priorities.

While it's impossible to attribute a campaign's success to a single variable, Stratton went on to best Krishnamoorthi by seven points and Kelly by 22.

Political food fights

At least one Republican adopted a similar bold strategy. In July, Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tennessee, released a controversial ad when she faced an unexpectedly competitive field of primary opponents to replace Gov. Bill Lee.

The two-term senator's gubernatorial campaign video featured Blackburn at a Chinese restaurant, surrounded by bottles of soy sauce and fortune cookies wrapped in plastic packaging.

"How hard am I going to crack down on China?" Blackburn says, flanked by red booths. "Well, here's a clue." The 74-year-old lawmaker then smashed a series of fortune cookies over a menu while grimacing. A piece of fortune cookie paper read, "MARSHA BLACKBURN WILL FIGHT TO PROTECT TENNESSEE LAND FROM CHINA."

Blackburn won the Aug. 6 primary by 10 points over her closest challenger.

Swing-state candidates look for broad appeal

As candidates in red and blue races double down on appealing to their base, candidates in competitive general election races are aiming to show their independence.

Pennsylvania's first-term Rep. Rob Bresnahan is defending a seat he won by less than two points in 2024 in a race rated "toss-up" by the nonpartisan Cook Political Report, which ranks political matchups across the country. (Balkcom, whose mom shot the intruder, faces Jamie Ager in a similar contest.)

He caught a bologna chub like a football in a new ad before slamming the meat log down on a kitchen island seemingly pulled straight out of ABC's 2000s suburban drama "Desperate Housewives."

"Paige Cognetti and her allies are full of baloney," Bresnahan says, referring to his Democratic opponent, the mayor of Joe Biden's hometown, Scranton. "Spending millions to paint me as something I am not."

In Iowa's toss-up Senate race, Rep. Ashley Hinson is creating space between herself and Trump – despite serving as a longtime surrogate – as she vies for the seat held by retiring Sen. Joni Ernst.

Ernst herself starred in a famous campaign commercial, "Squeal," in her first 2014 run for Senate in which she vowed to "make 'em squeal" after telling voters how she grew up castrating hogs.

In mid-September, Hinson's campaign released an ad featuring the congresswoman seated in a movie theater.

"It used to be that reaching across the aisle wasn't just OK, it was expected," Hinson says, as she handed over a bucket of popcorn across a theater aisle.

Monadnock Strategies founder Jesse Hunt, the former communications director at the Republican Governors Association, said campaigns target whatever group they need to win.

Democrat Josh Turek leads key Iowa Senate race, new poll shows

Sometimes, candidates woo base voters, Hunt said, and other times they seek support from independents like in Hinson's case.

"This might sound cliche, but it's all about what each campaign team believes is its winning coalition," Hunt said.

Hoops with Obama

Hinson's Democratic opponent, state Rep. Josh Turek, is running ads featuring Obama, who endorsed him in a basketball-themed July video. Obama, a noted basketball fan, shared his support for Turek, a two-time Paralympian in wheelchair basketball at the 2016 and 2020 Summer Games.

"Now, the ball's in your court," Obama says to Iowans.

Obama cut ads in October for a large slate of Democratic candidates in contentious races. He endorsed Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro for governor as well as Colorado's Phil Weiser, Wisconsin's David Crowley and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia who are competing in open gubernatorial contests.

He also endorsed Stratton, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Maine's Troy Jackson for Senate.

'I think most politicians are full of...'

In a swing district Trump won, one Democratic member of Congress is hoping to reuse unique tactics to distinguish her brand.

In 2024, Democratic state Sen. Kristen McDonald Rivet ran against Paul Junge in Michigan's 8th District, which became friendlier to Republicans after it was redrawn in 2023.

Now a congresswoman, Rivet enlisted the help of Declaration Media Group, a firm founded by Obama creative alumni who worked on successful battleground races in 2018 and 2020.

The Declaration team is again working with Rivet to win re-election in a district that includes Flint. The House member returned to a bar she filmed at during her first bid for Congress in a new ad.

"Two years ago, I sat right here and I told you this: 'I think most politicians are full of s---.' It's way worse than I thought," Rivet says.

"I approve this message because you deserve better than what you've been getting. I'm working hard to fix that," she adds while holding up a beer glass. A YouTube version posted Oct. 7 has nearly 1 million views.

Declaration consultants, including co-founder AJ Lenar, utilized Rivet's background in 2024 to separate her from national Democrats including then-President Joe Biden and Vice President Kamala Harris, who lost Michigan to Trump.

Last cycle, Lenar produced an ad where Rivet's husband threw himself out of a car. In the spot, the legislator obsesses over tax cuts on a neighborhood drive, so Joseph Rivet unbuckles his seatbelt and flings himself from the passenger seat of a red Chevrolet Impala.

"We knew that district was turning against us demographically, politically, right? And we just felt like we needed to do something that would make her stand out," Lenar told USA TODAY.

On Election Day, Rivet won by nearly 7 points while Trump prevailed over Harris by two percentage points in the district.

In an upcoming ad, Rivet's spouse will again reprise his role as sidekick – this time, Declaration applied special effects to set his hands on fire.

In the original bar spot, Declaration leaned into long held beliefs about sharing brews with officeholders.

"They say politics comes down to who you want to have a beer with, so here goes," Rivet says.

El-Sayed, Rogers clash: 4 takeaways from the Michigan Senate debate

Rivet, who used to run Michigan Head Start, also explains her biography: the lawmaker has six kids.

"I know, that's a lot," she says. "Now in the State Senate, I'm fighting to lower drug prices and housing costs and I helped pass the largest tax cut in state history."

"I root for the Lions, I hate Ohio and I think most politicians are full of s---," Rivet says. A beer glass slid into her right hand before she hoisted it up and said "Cheers!"

An ad standoff in Texas

Over 1,000 miles away from mid-Michigan, arguably no race has sparked more conversations about campaign advertising this cycle than the Texas Senate battle.

The Lone Star contest has been contentious since before the respective spring primaries determined Democratic state Rep. James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general, would become their parties' nominees.

Talarico released an opening ad standing on a rusted pickup truck, surrounded by dozens of people in front of a church. "The biggest divide in our country is not left vs. right, it's top vs. bottom," the Presbyterian seminarian says to cheers.

Rep. Jasmine Crockett, a two-term Dallas area congresswoman who also competed in the primaries, shared an announcement video in which she stares to the side as audio of Trump insulting her plays.

The contrasting ads stoked online narratives about both candidates – one of which was that Talarico was a man of the people while Crockett was more self-serving. Crockett lost the Senate primary to Talarico, her pre-congressional colleague in the statehouse, in March.

Then Talarico's campaign produced several ads to underscore Paxton's ethical dilemmas after Paxton prevailed in a May primary runoff over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn. In one August video, Talarico seized on Paxton taking a $1,000 Montblanc pen from a different man, lawyer Joe Joplin, in 2013 at the Collin County Courthouse.

The ad featured security footage ... and an endorsement from Joplin, the pen's owner.

Brandon Rottinghaus, a political science professor at the University of Houston, said Talarico's faith-based message has given his candidacy a distinctive identity. Talarico's campaign, Rottinghaus said, has cast him as a centrist who can appeal beyond the Democrats' national brand.

"He's able to present himself as somebody who's more moderate in a world that's very polarizing," Rottinghaus told USA TODAY.

Paxton is currently and very publicly estranged from his wife, state Sen. Angela Paxton. Recently, she starred in an early October ad that encouraged Republicans to vote red down the ticket.

Paxton's camp fought back, too. Their daughter, Mattie Hayworth Paxton, has appeared in multiple ads presenting her dad as a devoted father.

Texas is known for its uncertain terrain with its wetlands and deep canyons. The race's landscape is rough, too.

Rottinghaus said a win by Talarico could upend ideas about electability. He would be the first Texas Democrat to win a Senate seat since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

But his videos won't matter as much as votes on Nov. 3.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Guns, F-bombs, fortune cookies. What do wild campaign ads actually say?

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY at https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2026/10/15/campaign-ads-midterms-talarico-trump/92004345007/

item.title: Trump dismisses reports that White House chief of staff Susie Wiles's job is in jeopardy
item.description:
President Trump dismissed reporting that White House chief of staff Susie Wiles's job is in jeopardy Thursday. 

The White House issued a response from the president himself to Politico after the outlet reported that Trump has received negative feedback about Wiles from allies after soliciting their opinions about his chief of staff. 

“TOTAL FAKE NEWS Politico doesn’t care about facts, integrity, or honest journalism — it’s why I kicked them out of the White House!” Trump said in a statement to the outlet. “Susie Wiles is my loyal and longest serving Chief of Staff — there is a reason for that. She has been with me since the beginning, is my trusted advisor, and has my COMPLETE confidence. President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

Wiles is considered one of Trump’s most trusted advisers and confidants. She has played a major role in shaping his second administration and in securing his 2024 presidential victory as co-campaign manager. 

Trump has also publicly praised Wiles on numerous occasions. After Wiles announced that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer earlier this year, Trump referred to her as “an amazing person” and “an amazing fighter.” Wiles announced last month that she was cancer free. 

Politico’s reporting comes weeks after news surfaced that Trump political advisers James Blair and Chris LaCivita, who served as Wiles’s co-campaign manager in 2024, were paid to travel to the Balkans to advise a pro-Russian political party ahead of an election there. 

Trump said in a Truth Social post that he was not aware the two had taken the trip and that he would fire them if any wrongdoing took place.

据英国《泰晤士报》13日报道，英国军队已在马尔维纳斯群岛（简称马岛，英国称福克兰群岛）举行军事演习，模拟登陆作战，在阿根廷再次占领该岛的情况下夺回马岛控制权。报道指出，这是多年来英军首次举行包含两栖登陆在内的军事演习。


英军演练登陆夺取马岛 图源：英国皇家空军


据报道，9月27日至10月2日，英国陆军伞兵团第2营B连约150名士兵，与马岛防卫部队约100名当地预备役人员举行演习，部分内容是模仿1982年“萨顿行动”的登陆作战。一个伞兵排搭乘“梅德韦”号近海巡逻舰抵达马岛海岸，换乘充气式登陆艇上岸，完成约32公里夜间行军后，在英国空军“台风”战斗机支援下对目标阵地发动拂晓突袭，随后由直升机运送部队继续推进，展开近距离攻击并夺取目标阵地。


英国国防部称，士兵在不到3小时内推进数英里，并“消灭该地区所有敌人”。演习指挥官农库辛说，虽然演习再现历史战斗场景，但也为适配新型战争的需求进行了调整，还研究了网络、太空领域带来的影响，模拟遭遇无人机袭击，找出战术、技术和流程上的短板。


《泰晤士报》称，英军通常每三个月模拟马岛战争时的战况开展演习，但已多年未举行登陆夺岛演练。英国国防消息人士强调，此次演习属于计划内活动，并非针对阿根廷方面近期言论的临时反应。


阿根廷和英国对马岛主权存在争议。1982年阿英两国因马岛主权归属问题爆发战争，并以英国胜利而告终。阿根廷总统米莱在9月21日表示，不会以军事手段解决马岛主权争端，将坚持寻求外交途径收复马岛主权。另外，阿根廷已就英国公司与以色列公司合作的“海狮”油田项目诉诸国际仲裁。

item.title: 老人替孙子尝了口“白桃饮料”，食道遭灼烧，被紧急送医洗胃……医生提醒
item.description:
近日

云南宾川县金牛镇一名老人

因家中清洁剂瓶身与饮料相似

误将“白桃香氛洁厕慕斯”

当成饮料尝了一口

随后出现

口腔、咽喉麻涩及食道烧灼感



爷爷替孙子尝饮料误服洁厕慕斯


事发时

老人独自在家照看孙子

孩子从卫生间柜子里翻出

一个粉色、印有水蜜桃图案的瓶子

以为是饮料想喝

老人因担心饮料过期

便想着先尝一口

没想到入口后感觉不对

戴上老花镜仔细查看才发现

瓶中装的是洁厕慕斯

家人得知后 立即将老人送医



所幸老人误服量不多

也没有让孩子饮用

经救治后顺利出院

小编发现

此前有网友评论

该产品包装、味道容易混淆


网友评论截图


清洁剂包装“仿饮料”暗藏风险

而生活中还有一种更危险的习惯

不少人为图方便

把清洁剂倒进空饮料瓶分装

一旦混淆 后果更加严重


宁波女子误服空调清洗剂

致食管、胃部大面积溃疡


9月29日 浙江宁波镇海

46岁的李女士把空调清洗剂

分装在空饮料瓶

自己却不小心当成饮料误饮

强碱成分瞬间灼伤消化道

造成食管、胃部大面积溃疡

经过一个月的系统治疗才好转出院


视频来源 宁波晚报


不仅成年人存在误服风险

好奇心强、辨识能力弱的幼儿

更是这类危险化学品的高危人群


2岁男童误把家中百草枯当饮料喝下

送ICU急救


近日

内蒙古2岁男童小宇在家玩耍时

误将百草枯当饮料喝下

没过多久 小宇就出现呕吐等症状

送医后 小宇被紧急转入儿童重症医学科

经过多日抢救 小宇顺利出院



万一误喝

避开四大急救误区


误服危险化学品事发突然

一旦意外发生

错误的急救操作会加重伤害

掌握正确急救方法至关重要


医生提醒，万一误喝，首要动作是立刻停止继续吞咽；可用少量清水反复漱口，清理口腔残留的腐蚀性液体；伤者保持静坐或侧躺姿势，防范腐蚀液体反流，避免食道受到二次损伤。


四大急救误区务必避开，错误操作会加重伤情，甚至危及生命：


  • 严禁抠喉催吐。呕吐会让腐蚀物反流，再次灼伤食道，严重时可能造成食道穿孔。

  • 禁止大量灌水稀释。大量饮水不仅会产生热量加重消化道灼伤，还极易诱发呕吐，造成二次伤害。

  • 不要喝牛奶、蛋清、油脂类物质。这类黏稠液体容易包裹腐蚀剂，掩盖体内损伤程度，耽误医生诊断治疗。

  • 切勿尝试酸碱中和。醋、小苏打、肥皂水等中和剂，会和腐蚀剂发生化学反应释放大量热量，加重消化道黏膜溃烂。


一旦伤者出现口腔麻木刺痛、咽喉肿痛、吞咽困难、胸口及食道烧灼痛、不停流口水、声音嘶哑、恶心呕吐、胸闷憋气等任一症状，要马上拨打120急救电话。


送医时，请带上原装瓶，方便医护人员快速判断腐蚀成分，及时开展针对性救治。


急救知识记住了

但最好的办法 是防患于未然



✔️购买清洁剂时，尽量不要选择包装过度像零食饮料的产品；


✔️绝对不要把消毒液、清洁剂二次倒进饮料瓶分装，一定要保留原标签原瓶；


✔️所有卫生间、厨房等清洁剂，收纳在专门存放地点、带柜门的高处，避免孩子拿得到。老年人容易拿混，最好和食品、饮料分开存放；


✔️千万不要靠尝一口，去判断能不能吃、有没有过期，入口之前一定要看清说明标签。

item.title: 教师不愿当班主任，困局从何处破解
item.description:
钟煜豪

班主任，正成为部分省份中小学教师职称晋升的硬性门槛。

其中，今年9月1日起实施的《湖南省中小学教师系列职称评价办法》明确：申报一级教师需担任班主任工作2年以上，申报高级教师需担任班主任工作4年以上，申报正高级教师需担任班主任工作5年以上。

就此，湖南宁乡市教育局10月14日进一步解释称，根据上级部门职称工作会议精神，为确保新旧政策平稳衔接，对班主任工作年限相关要求设置一年过渡期，2026年度职称评审，班主任工作年限不作为职称申报硬性准入门槛，不因未达规定班主任年限而直接否决申报资格。2027年度职称评审，班主任工作年限将作为申报中高级教师的必要条件严格执行，未达相应年限要求的，将不再受理申报。

班主任被视为班级的“灵魂”，肩负着班级工作的组织者、学生成长的引领者、家校社协同的桥梁等多重角色。但在当前，因班主任工作负荷重、压力大、专业性要求高，导致许多教师担任意愿不强，部分学校不得不安排新入职教师直接承担班主任职责。湖南的做法是，将班主任工作经历由“加分项”调整为职称评审的“硬门槛”。

《中国教育报》新近报道就提到，此举开始改变教师不愿当班主任的困局。今年秋季新学期，湖南多地中小学班主任岗位出现了从“冷”到“热”的显著变化。在新化县田坪镇茶溪中学，连续担任班主任7年的曹女全今年新学期第一次“卸任”了班主任，因为主动报名的老师明显增多。在常德市鼎城区草坪镇芙蓉学校，新学期班主任工作安排的难度大大降低。张家界武陵源区协合乡某小学也出现了年轻教师主动请缨担任班主任的情况。

近些年，多地陆续强化评价激励导向，增强班主任的职业吸引力。例如，有的在奖励性绩效工资、绩效考核奖分配中对班主任予以重点倾斜，有的在职称评聘、评优评先中将班主任工作年限和业绩作为重要评价指标。还有地方人大代表、政协委员提出，有条件的学校可探索推行教管分离，将班主任从学科教学中分离出来，进行独立的考核和评价。这些，都映照出班主任工作的复杂性。

也有不容忽视的观点认为，部分一线教师虽教学业绩突出，但因未担任班主任而被硬性否决，实际贡献可能被忽视，容易造成评价标准单一化。还有人担忧，如果成为刚性红线，很可能滋生为了获任班主任而私下运作的不良风气，这既背离了政策初衷，也可能影响班主任队伍的整体质量。

关于班主任队伍建设的各项政策及配套细则，需要动态完善，防止其异化为“晋升跳板”。一方面，对于确实因学科特点、学校安排等原因未能担任班主任的教师，应开辟合理的替代性评价通道。如湖南就明确担任少先队辅导员、心理健康教育、德育、课后服务或学生管理工作的教师工作年限可按班主任工作年限计算。

另一方面，更要继续推进班主任待遇提升、工作减负、专业培训和评价机制改革，通过日趋丰富的激励政策让教师们真心愿意去当班主任，而不是为了职称、为了熬够年限“不得不”当班主任。唯有如此，才能让班主任从“职称刚需”走向“职业自觉”。说到底，要让班主任真正成为令人向往的岗位，不能只靠职称评审的“大棒”，还有赖更多的“胡萝卜”。只有多管齐下、标本兼治，才能从根本上破解“不愿当班主任”的难题。


本期编辑 陆枫

item.title: 釜山升格A类首位华语影后！周迅哽咽感谢父母，鼓励拥抱变化
item.description:
澎湃新闻记者 刘雨濛

10月15日晚，第31届釜山国际电影节，中国演员周迅凭借电影《初次尝到寂寞》中“江月”一角，摘得最佳演员奖，这也是釜山电影节在今年升格为国际A类电影节后，在其主竞赛单元诞生的第一位华语影后。该片同时斩获艺术贡献奖，场刊拿到3.7分/4分，位列评分第一。

釜山电影节红毯上的周迅

颁奖礼上，周迅从萨梅尔·叶斯利亚莫娃和张东健手中接过奖杯，台下坐着的中国电影人张艺谋、舒淇和毕赣等共同见证。当周迅说到感谢父母给她生命和自由、让她成为自己时，声音一度哽咽。她还说道已经做了30多年的演员，在现在这个年龄段，能感受到生命中非常多的变化。“有一些可以欣然接受，有一些也很期待，但是有一些变化是没有办法承受的悲伤。”周迅鼓励大家在面对这些沉重的变化时，可以有拥抱它的勇气，要有一定会转向正面的信心。

电影《初次尝到寂寞》是导演顾游“山水电影三部曲”的收官之作，也是本届釜山电影节主竞赛单元唯一入围的华语长片。影片以一场至亲离别为叙事切口，串联起三代女性在生死与和解过程中的各自体悟。周迅在片中出演历经人生起落的中年女性江月，她以“克制而内敛”的表演，将角色在别离中的厚重情绪，层层铺展。

周迅曾凭借在《如果·爱》《李米的猜想》里的精彩表演，成为首位“三金”满贯的华语影后。如今，再添一座A类电影节影后桂冠，让人始终觉得，无论时光如何流转，她的表演自带一股难以言说的灵气。圈内好友陈坤、辛芷蕾也第一时间向她表示了祝贺。

辛芷蕾向周迅表示祝贺。



本期编辑 陆枫

item.title: 分析：特朗普让通胀重返美国中西部地区，农村受害最深
item.description:
农村地区受到更严重冲击，主要与柴油和汽油等机动车燃料价格有关。这些燃料的价格同比上涨了35%。 根据美国劳工统计局的消费者支出调查，机动车燃料在农村家庭支出中所占的比例远高于城市家庭。 此外，农村家庭对取暖和烹饪燃料的依赖程度也明显更高，而这类燃料的价格已经上涨44%，其中包括煤油和丙烷。 在传统电网和天然气管网覆盖不到的地区，居民需要依靠这些燃料为住宅供暖、加热生活用水和烹饪。这种情况在美国中西部、大平原地区以及阿巴拉契亚山脉部分地区尤其常见。 尽管特朗普大力宣扬自己与普京达成了一项允许俄罗斯出口柴油的协议，但普遍看法是，协议涉及的数量太少，不足以压低价格。甚至连特朗普所在共和党的政治人物也不赞成这项安排。 农村选民是共和党的重要票仓。2024年总统选举中，69%的农村选民支持特朗普，只有29%支持民主党候选人哈里斯。这是特朗普参加的三次总统大选中，农村选民支持率差距最大的一次。 虽然农村社区人口只占美国总人口的五分之一，但在决定参议院的席位构成方面，农村选民拥有远超人口比例的影响力。

item.title: 霸王龙为什么长着迷你的前肢
item.description:
2026-10-15 23:00:00

霸王龙的形象极具反差感，一方面有着巨大的脑袋和锋利的牙齿，另一方面也有着迷你的前肢。这双短小得连自己的嘴巴都够不到的奇特小爪子，长期困扰着古生物学家：恐龙界的顶尖霸主为什么会演化出这样一对看上去似乎毫无用处的小爪子？

霸王龙。视觉中国|插画

头骨越强大，前肢越短小

其实这种短前肢的现象，并不是霸王龙的专属特征。2026年5月，《英国皇家学会学报B辑：生物科学》刊发了一项最新研究，为解开这个谜题提供了一种解释。

伦敦大学学院与剑桥大学的科研团队，把目光投向整个兽脚类恐龙大家族，分析了85种恐龙的化石资料。他们发现，前肢大幅缩短并不是偶然事件，霸王龙所属的暴龙科，以及鲨齿龙科、阿贝力龙科、角鼻龙科、斑龙科等五个完全不同的演化分支，都独立出现了前肢退化变短的情况。

特别是阿贝力龙科、鲨齿龙科以及暴龙科，前肢相比头骨的缩短幅度尤其大。这一结果说明，短小的前肢并不是某一类恐龙独有的标记。不同顶级肉食恐龙虽分布在世界不同地方，但都选择了缩小前肢的演化生存策略。

那么，究竟是什么力量，推动着不同恐龙反复出现这样的演化变化？过去有一种很普遍的看法，认为这只是恐龙身体巨型化带来的附带结果，整体体型变大，四肢相对就显得短小。但最新研究发现了更多的关联。研究人员整合了头骨特点、牙齿形态、咬合力等多方面的数据，搭建起了一套可以衡量头骨坚固程度的评估体系。分析之后发现：前肢的退化程度与头骨的坚固程度高度相关。这种关联，甚至比恐龙体重增加带来的影响还要突出。

简单来说，决定前肢长短的关键，不在于这只恐龙体型究竟多大，而在于它的头骨够不够结实、咬合力有多强悍。有研究测算，霸王龙的咬合力可达35000牛顿，和其他动物拉开巨大差距；对比之下，人类咬合力通常不超过1000牛顿。按照最新研究对头骨坚固程度的评估标准，霸王龙的头骨坚固度在所有被研究的恐龙里也是排名第一。

研究团队推测，捕猎的核心武器，慢慢从前肢转移到了头骨。当恐龙的咬合力足够强悍，一口就能给猎物造成致命伤害，原本用来抓握、撕扯猎物的前肢，作用就不断下降，慢慢变成了可有可无的部位。

关于资源取舍的博弈

这一切的源头，可能来自一场持续数百万年的演化“军备竞赛”。当时，像蜥脚类、角龙类这样的植食恐龙，体型越变越大，也越来越难捕猎。对于肉食恐龙来说，想要靠爪子去牵制一头体长三十米的巨型蜥脚类恐龙，几乎很难实现；依靠强有力的颌部直接撕咬攻击，看起来才是更高效的捕猎方式。

它们或许因此放弃了用前肢和嘴来协同猎捕的模式，转而把身体有限的资源，全部倾斜到升级头部与颌部这套主力武器上，逐渐拥有了更有力量的头骨。不过，生物自身所能调动的能量和资源终究是有限的，既要撑起一颗硕大沉重的头颅，又要维持一对强壮有力的前肢，会消耗海量的能量。当头部已经成为捕猎的核心武器之后，修长健壮的前肢非但带不来生存优势，还会消耗大量能量，打乱身体重心，近身搏斗时更容易受伤，反而成为负担。

相较之下，前肢更短小轻便的个体，则更具生存优势。节省下来的能量，可以供给头部和咬合系统，进一步强化捕猎能力。这就是自然选择的逻辑：当头部演化成终极杀伤性武器，前肢变得小巧，并不是演化留下的缺陷，而是权衡利弊之后做出的生存选择。

这项研究也再次验证了自然演化中一条很重要的规律：生物身上任何一项优势，都建立在资源分配的取舍之上。顶尖掠食者，并不是所有器官都十全十美；很多时候，舍弃某项能力，才能把另一项能力打磨到极致。虽然目前还无法确定这中间的因果关系，但研究人员估计，前肢较短的恐龙应该是先演化出强悍结实的头骨，之后前肢才慢慢缩短。否则没有其他可用的捕猎手段，就直接丢掉原本的进攻器官，在演化逻辑上不合理。

换句话说，前肢退化，并不是恐龙主动抛弃了自己的爪子，而是头部的作战能力足够强大之后，前肢成了冗余器官，才被自然选择一步步“精简”。这种“先升级核心装备，再弱化多余结构”的过程，也证明演化不是漫无目的的变化，而是生物在生存压力下，一步步摸索出来的最优生存方案。

演化的底层逻辑

当然，兽脚类恐龙的演化，并不只有这一种成功路线。棘龙、部分巨盗龙，就走出了完全不一样的道路。它们保留了修长的前肢与巨大的爪，搭配的却是偏细长的头骨。这套身体结构，说明它们占据着不一样的生存生态位，比如捕鱼、捕捉小型猎物，并不像霸王龙那样专门正面猎杀巨型植食恐龙。

由此不难看出，捕食对象和捕猎方式，会深刻改变掠食动物的身体构造。若是不同捕食者都以同一类大型猎物为食，它们的头骨、牙齿、四肢，就很有可能演化出趋同的特征；可一旦食物来源不一样，身体结构也会出现巨大差别。这恰恰展现了恐龙演化的丰富多样性，不同的演化分支，抓住各自的生存机遇，发展出独属于自己的身体本领。

另外值得注意的是，霸王龙这对短小的前肢，虽然小，并不是完全没用。曾有研究推测，它能完成辅助起身这类特定动作。化石上留下的前肢受力痕迹、骨折之后愈合的印记，都能证明，这个部位依旧要承受不小的力。

恐龙，可以说是地球上最擅长适应、演化花样层出不穷的动物。霸王龙这对看着滑稽的小前肢，没有削弱其陆地霸主的实力，反倒成为我们理解趋同演化、器官权衡、生态适应的绝佳样本，背后更是一系列关于身体能量分配、生存博弈的演化规律。

item.title: FBI investigates suspicious mail sent to Senate and election offices
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal authorities are investigating letters with “suspicious substances” that have been mailed to congressional and election offices nationwide and are urging recipients to treat the mailings as “potentially hazardous.”

The investigation by the FBI, U.S. Postal Inspection Service and U.S. Capitol Police was first disclosed in a message from the Senate Sergeant at Arms obtained Thursday by The Associated Press. The notice, sent to Senate offices, said that law enforcement officials were working to intercept any additional letters, but “it is possible that some letters may reach their destinations.”

In Congress, the threat appeared limited to the Senate, though the House was monitoring the situation, according to a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to discuss the investigation publicly.

An FBI statement said the bureau and the Postal Inspection Service were "investigating a series of suspicious mailings sent to various addresses nationwide, including Secretary of State offices and their related election offices.”

"Some of the letters contained an unknown substance and we are working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident," the statement read. "We are also working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters."

Mailed packages containing a powdery substance led to the evacuation this week of election offices in at least two states, Louisiana and Oklahoma. The Ohio secretary of state said the Postal Service intercepted a package containing a white powder intended for its office and noted that similar mailings had been sent to election officials in multiple states. Numerous states, from Idaho to Florida, said their election offices either received letters or had them intercepted by the Postal Service.

The Wisconsin Elections Commission said in a statement that it received a letter and the white powder enclosed in it as not hazardous, according to tests. "Let this be very clear: this incident will not shake us,” Wisconsin elections administrator Meagan Wolfe said.

News of the letters comes just three weeks before Election Day and is reminiscent of a similar threat in 2023, when election offices in six states received mailings that contained a white powder. In some cases, the incidents disrupted work around local elections.

Some of those letters contained threats and traces of the powerful opioid fentanyl, leading some election offices to stock up on the overdose reversal medication naloxone.

The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors issued a joint statement condemning what they said were threats against election staff.

“Those who administer our elections should never fear for their safety while carrying out their essential duties,” they said in their statement.

Deputy Postal Inspector Brendan Donahue told reporters Thursday that “any threat or attack on election officials is unacceptable” and that “we are also working with our partners on identifying the individual or individuals responsible for the letters.”

___

Associated Press writers Scott Bauer in Madison, Wisconsin; Sarah Rankin in Richmond, Virginia; and Nicholas Riccardi in Denver contributed to this report.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/fbi-postal-investigating-letters-suspicious-152513309.html

item.title: 以色列公司通过数字广告安装零点击间谍软件
item.description: 加拿大多伦多大学公民实验室发表研究报告，以色列公司 Discover-Tech 通过数字广告在半岛电视台的内部设备上安装了间谍软件。这是首次利用数字广告实施的零点击间谍软件攻击。Discover-Tech 运营着名为 Controlium 的平台，它表面上是一家合法的广告公司，但实际上是以色列间谍软件供应商的合作伙伴。Controlium 能在广告加载的瞬间，对设备进行去匿名化处理、提取设备指纹，自动植入恶意软件。对 Discover-Tech 四十亿条竞价记录的分析显示，在四个月时间里，该公司的广告出现在数十个国家、近 20 万个不同的网站及 Android/iOS 应用中。公民实验室称，名为 DARK CARTOGRAPHER 的组织正利用 Discover-Tech 的基础设施，通过挖掘多家移动运营商系统中的漏洞，将设备的广告标识符与电话号码进行关联，对互联网用户实施大规模的去匿名化。Google 等已采取行动，切断了 Discover-Tech 接入数字广告生态系统的渠道。

item.title: 美国银行雇佣千名合同工修复 AI 工具发现的软件漏洞
item.description: 美国银行（Bank of America）CEO Brian Moynihan 透露该公司雇佣了千名合同工帮助修复 Anthropic Mythos 等 AI 工具发现的软件漏洞。他表示：“我们在第二季度聘请了 1000 名合同工协助进行修复工作。除了原本负责该领域的 3000 名员外，这些合同工至今仍留在公司内，继续提供协助。”他向分析师透露，美国银行第三季度在软件修复以及与反洗钱合规相关的监管问题上投入了数亿美元以上的资金。这是美国大型企业首次披露其为保护软件系统免受 Mythos 影响所投入的人力和资金规模。

item.title: 受混合动力汽车协议鼓舞，欧洲各国就对华采取更强硬立场达成共识
item.description: 南华早报消息，在成功说服中国接受一项将其对欧州混动汽车出口限制在每年 35 万辆的协议后，布鲁塞尔深受鼓舞，如今正发动引擎，准备在一系列单边行动上提速。

item.title: 民主党民调支持率上升，共和党投入重金加大中期选举广告攻势
item.description:
在另一些选区，随着共和党候选人的胜选前景恶化，负责共和党参议院竞选事务的机构已经开始撤回资金，包括北卡罗来纳州和佐治亚州的选举。 特朗普在2024年总统选举中以超过3个百分点的优势赢得北卡罗来纳州，但目前这个州的民主党参议员候选人已经领先共和党对手10个百分点。 共和党还从少数几个众议院选区撤走了部分竞选资金。 不过，随着竞选进入最后几周，其他竞争激烈的选区仍在获得两党大量资金投入。 德克萨斯州参议员选举吸引的广告资金尤其惊人。包括党内初选和正式选举在内，这场竞选的广告支出已经超过5.03亿美元，是本轮中期选举中广告投入最高的一场竞争。 过去三周，共和党在德克萨斯州的广告支出激增131%，达到2.32亿美元。 根据美国政治民调汇总网站RealClearPolitics的最新数据，民主党候选人詹姆斯·塔拉里科目前领先共和党对手肯·帕克斯顿约3个百分点。 帕克斯顿是德克萨斯州总检察长，长期受到各种丑闻困扰。特朗普今年5月宣布支持他。

来源

item.title: 华邮曝光特朗普白宫宴会厅捐款名单：筹资3.33亿美元，英伟达等多家企业出钱后获得政府合同和监管批准
item.description:
《华盛顿邮报》获得的内部文件显示，特朗普白宫宴会厅项目已从私人捐款人处筹集3.33亿美元，其中至少7700万美元来自要求匿名的捐款人。英伟达、苹果、共和党金主阿德尔森家族及电信富豪厄根各承诺捐赠2500万美元。约一半捐款来自特朗普第二任期内获得联邦政府合同的企业及相关高管。 调查发现，多名大额捐款人在捐款前后获得政府合同、监管批准或其他有利决定。英伟达在获得向中国销售先进芯片的许可后捐款；厄根旗下企业在监管调查终止后承诺捐款；赛富时在捐款期间获得最高价值56亿美元的陆军合同。另有捐款人的父亲获得特朗普赦免。 这项筹款活动因缺乏透明度引发利益输送质疑。部分工程费用实际上已由纳税人承担。

来源

item.title: 菲律宾外交部驳斥中国驻菲大使井泉对马尼拉“动武”的威胁
item.description: 菲律宾外交部星期四(10月15日)发表声明，指责中国驻菲律宾大使井泉在向媒体发表谈话时用词不当，向马尼拉传递出一种“不加掩饰”的武力威胁。

item.title: 巴基斯坦学校屋顶坍塌32学童和一名女教师遇难 社区居民要求彻查劣质建材
item.description: 周四，巴基斯坦北部白沙瓦一所学校的屋顶坍塌，造成32名儿童和一名女教师遇难。事发后，救援人员和遇难者家属赶往现场，试图营救遇难者。

item.title: Could this be the year Democrats close the 'governor gap' with Republicans?
item.description:
When people talk about this year's midterms, they tend to focus on whether Democrats will end unified Republican control of Congress by winning the U.S. Senate or House of Representatives (or both). And that makes sense: Congress has the power to check President Trump's agenda, so the national repercussions could be huge. 

But on Election Day, there will be something else to watch out for: whether Democrats can emerge with more governors' mansions than Republicans.  

GOP governors have outnumbered their Democratic counterparts for the last 15 years straight (and for 26 of the last 30 years overall). That's given Republicans more opportunities to experiment with new policy ideas, approve congressional maps, influence election procedures, fill Senate vacancies and build executive experience.

But this year, Democrats have a real shot at closing the "governor gap." They need to net one governorship to tie Republicans at 25; net two, and they'll secure a gubernatorial "majority" for the first time since 2011. At the moment, 16 of this year's 36 gubernatorial contests are considered competitive, according to the expert race handicappers at the nonpartisan Cook Political Report — and 11 of them are in Republican-held states. 

So Democrats are on offense. It remains to be seen, however, whether they will actually overcome decades of GOP gubernatorial dominance in places like Alaska, Georgia, Iowa, Ohio and Texas on Nov. 3. Here are the races to watch.

Alaska

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Bernadette Wilson

The Democrat: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins 

Alaska hasn't elected a Democratic governor in 28 years. But that could change on Nov. 3 as Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins — known locally as JKT — has emerged as the frontrunner to succeed term-limited GOP Gov. Mike Dunleavy. In part, that's due to the Last Frontier's unique voting system, which sends the top four primary candidates to the general election regardless of party — then asks voters to rank them on Election Day in order of preference, from first to fourth. As a result, Kreiss-Tomkins, a 37-year-old former state representative, is the only Democrat competing against three Republicans: conservative activist Bernadette Wilson, former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson and former state Attorney General Treg Taylor. 

But economic dissatisfaction, Trump's low approval ratings in the state and Kreiss-Tomkins's energetic campaign are also helping to boost Democratic hopes. Recent polls suggest Kreiss-Tomkins could win the first round of ranked-choice balloting with nearly 50% of the vote — roughly twice as much as the second-place candidate (Wilson). On Oct. 13, Cook shifted its race rating from "toss up" to "lean Democrat." Along with Iowa, the outlet wrote, Alaska "may be Democrats' best opportunity to flip a governors' mansion in a red state." 

Florida

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Byron Donalds

The Democrat: David Jolly

A former swing state, Florida has trended increasingly Republican during the Trump era. The governor's mansion, however, has been red ever since Jeb Bush won the job in 1998. U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds — the third Black Republican in history to represent the Sunshine State on Capitol Hill — is seeking to keep the GOP's streak alive by succeeding term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis. His opponent is Democrat David Jolly, a former Republican congressman who left the GOP during Trump's first term. 

The president endorsed Donalds, a staunch social conservative, before he even entered the race; in Congress, Donalds has closely aligned himself with Trump's MAGA policies, especially on immigration. Meanwhile, Jolly is emphasizing his Christian faith, his conversion from Republican to independent to Democrat and his approach to key local issues like homeowner's insurance (which involves creating a state-backed catastrophe fund to keep costs down). 

Recent polls mostly show Donalds — who has raised more than seven times as much money as Jolly — leading by single-digit margins, with less than 50% of the vote; a few suggest a tie. Cook rates the race as "lean Republican." 

Georgia

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Rick Jackson

The Democrat: Keisha Lance Bottoms

Georgia has become the purplest of purple states in recent years: Trump lost it by 0.2 percentage points in 2020 and won it by 2 points in 2024. But while Georgians have sent two Democrats to the U.S. Senate in recent years — Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff — they haven't elected a Democratic governor since 1998. 

Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms has a chance to break the pattern on Nov. 3. The polls show her within striking distance — anywhere from 1 to 3 percentage points — of health care billionaire Rick Jackson, who won the GOP nomination without Trump's endorsement. Both candidates are promising to lower the cost of living by lowering taxes — a mainstream message in a relatively centrist state. Jackson has a huge financial edge, but Cook still rates the race as a toss up.  

If elected, Bottoms would make history as Georgia's first woman governor and the first Black woman governor anywhere in the U.S. 

Iowa

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Zach Lahn

The Democrat: Rob Sand

Iowa is another state that hasn't elected a Democratic governor in decades — 20 years to be exact. But state auditor Rob Sand, 44, has led in every poll conducted this cycle, often by double-digit margins. 

As auditor — and before that, as Iowa's assistant attorney general — Sand developed a reputation as a "happy warrior for nonpartisan technocratic efficiency and anti-corruption," a leading progressive activist recently told the Atlantic. He has also downplayed his allegiance to the national Democratic Party, calling it "the lesser of two evils." Such positioning has made Sand perhaps the most popular politician in a state where registered Republicans outnumber Democrats by almost 200,000.

Sand's opponent, businessman Zach Lahn, narrowly upset Trump's pick, Rep. Randy Feenstra, in this summer's Republican primary. A Kansas resident until 2023, Lahn has struggled to overcome accusations of carpetbagging ever since. Cook says the race "leans Democrat" and describes it as the party's best pickup opportunity.

Kansas

Party control: Democratic

The Republican: Ty Masterson 

The Democrat: Cindy Holscher 

Kansas is anything but a blue state; since 1940, it has voted Republican in every presidential election but one — Lyndon B. Johnson's 1964 landslide. But the Sunflower State has elected two Democratic women governors in recent years: Kathleen Sebelius (2003-2009) and term-limited incumbent Laura Kelly (2019-2027). State Sen. Cindy Holscher is seeking to become the third. 

Holscher has her work cut out for her, though. She's up against Ty Masterson, the president of the state Senate, who leads by a few percentage points in most recent polls. Cook rates the Kansas contest as "lean Republican," making it this year's only potential blue-to-red flip with that rating.

If Masterson does win in November, it wouldn't be particularly surprising. Since 1957, neither major political party has held the Kansas governor's mansion for longer than eight consecutive years.

Nevada 

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Joe Lombardo

The Democrat: Aaron Ford

Incumbent GOP Gov. Joe Lombardo — the former sheriff of Clark County — won in 2022 on a law-and-order message. But Nevada is a swing state, and Lombardo's insistence on vetoing a raft of affordability bills passed by the Democratic legislature — to cap the cost of prescription drugs; to provide paid family leave to workers; to prohibit private equity and big banks from buying up housing en masse; to continue universal free breakfast and lunch for K-12 schoolchildren — has become a source of criticism in a cycle often centered on the cost of living. And his previous support for data-center subsidies hasn't helped. 

Enter state Attorney General Aaron Ford, who is running on his working-class roots. Only two polls have been conducted since Labor Day. One shows Ford ahead by 2 points; the other shows Lombardo leading by 2. Cook rates the race a "toss up." 

Ohio

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Vivek Ramaswamy

The Democrat: Amy Acton

On paper, the odds are against Amy Acton, a Democrat who previously served as Ohio's chief public health officer. In 2024, Trump won the Buckeye State by the widest presidential margin since Ronald Reagan — more than 11 percentage points — and Democrats have lost all but one gubernatorial contest there since 1990. 

But most recent polls have shown Acton leading billionaire pharmaceutical and biotech entrepreneur (and former GOP presidential candidate) Vivek Ramaswamy — often by a decent margin. And while the race has been one of the "ugliest in the country," according to a recent New York Times report — "with exaggerated portrayals of one candidate as a con artist and the other as a drunk" — voters there continue to hold a narrowly favorable view of Acton and a narrowly unfavorable view of Ramaswamy.

Cook rates Ohio as a "toss up." 

Texas 

Party control: GOP

The Republican: Greg Abbott

The Democrat: Gina Hinojosa

Greg Abbott has been governor of Texas since 2015. Before that, he was Texas attorney general for more than a dozen years. He's perhaps the most familiar Republican politician in a state where Republicans have long dominated politics.

But even Abbott is at risk this cycle. Beyond the overall environment — which favors Democrats — the governor has faced backlash over Flock cameras, school privatization, data centers and his close ties to Trump. (Abbott skipped the president's campaign stop in San Antonio last week, saying he had a scheduling conflict.) He's also facing a strong challenger in Gina Hinojosa, who has pitched herself as more "populist" than "progressive." 

The latest polls show Abbott and Hinojosa trading small leads ahead of Election Day. Cook says the race "leans Republican."

Wisconsin

Party control: Democratic

The Republican: Tom Tiffany

The Democrat: David Crowley

After Gov. Tony Evers declined to seek a third term, democratic socialist Francesca Hong emerged as the frontrunner to win Wisconsin's Democratic primary in August. Milwaukee County executive David Crowley dropped out in mid-July — then re-entered the race 10 days later. With Evers's endorsement, he was able to edge Hong for the nod. 

The idea behind Crowley's last-minute comeback was that he would be more electable than Hong, who raised eyebrows with her past statements calling for the U.S. to "cancel" Thanksgiving and "abolish" the police. Recent polling has been consistent with that theory, showing Crowley consistently leading U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany — but only by single-digit margins. Cook rates the race a "toss up.".

If elected, Crowley would be Wisconsin's first Black governor.

The rest 

According to Cook, there are three states where Democrats currently hold the governorship that could be considered competitive: Arizona (Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs vs. Republican U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs); Oregon (Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek vs. Republican state Sen. Christine Drazan); and Michigan (Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson vs. Republican U.S. Rep. John James). Cook rates all three as "lean Democratic." 

Cook also recently moved three states from "solid Republican" to "likely Republican," reflecting movement toward the Democratic candidate. They are Nebraska (Republican Gov. Jim Pillen vs. Democratic former state Sen. Lynne Walz); Oklahoma (Republican former state Sen. Mike Mazzei vs. Democratic state Rep. Cyndi Munson); and Vermont (Republican Gov. Phil Scott vs. Democratic economist Amanda Janoo).

A fourth Republican-held state, New Hampshire, is also in the "likely Republican" category. GOP Gov. Kelly Ayotte is facing Democratic former executive councilor Cinde Warmington.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/article/could-this-be-the-year-democrats-close-the-governor-gap-with-republicans-180815424.html

item.title: Secret documents reveal donors behind $330 million for Trump's ballroom
item.description:
A list obtained by The Washington Post reveals all the major donors to President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom project, including previously undisclosed contributors who have benefited from regulatory decisions, government contracts and, in one case, a pardon for a family member.

Tech giants Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million, the top contribution amount, the list shows. The Adelson family, one of the GOP’s largest donor dynasties, committed that sum as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network.

Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post.

Absent from the list is Trump himself, who has said that he is helping to pay for the project. “It’s being paid for a hundred percent by me and some friends of mine,” he said last year, days after demolition began on the old East Wing.

The White House publicly identified 37 people, companies and foundations as donors last October, without revealing the amount of their individual gifts.

The list obtained by The Post, an internal spreadsheet used to track contributions for the fundraising effort, contains the source, date and amount of all 67 donations above $10,000 recorded as of late last month. It shows a total of $333 million from private donors, aligning with the administration’s public statements. Additional records, also internal to the fundraising effort, provide more detail about the donations and indicate that at least $77 million came from donors who requested anonymity.

The list and other documents offer a panoramic view of a fundraising campaign that is extraordinary both for its size and opacity. Ordinary political giving requires public disclosure and is subject to campaign finance rules. The ballroom donations are collected by a nonprofit and then channeled to the government and into a White House account the president directly controls.

Independent experts and scholars have expressed alarm at the potential the arrangement has for influence buying and coerced giving.

Some donors on the list obtained by The Post cut large checks, while others created installment plans that are still being paid off, the additional records show. The list does not include in-kind contributions.

The Post’s reporting does not establish a connection between the donation commitments and favorable actions by the Trump administration. But the documents show that the vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government.

Companies or executives of firms that have had contracts with the federal government during Trump’s second term accounted for about half of the total, The Post found.

After reviewing the list obtained by The Post, White House spokesman Davis Ingle declined to discuss individual donations but described the ballroom donors as “a wide array of great American companies and generous individuals, all of whom are contributing to make the People’s House better for generations to come.”

“The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests, would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations,” he said. He added that the administration will “relentlessly pursue those responsible for this cowardly leak while continuing to protect all those who give.”

The Post is publishing the names of the 57 donors listed as having committed to giving $100,000 or more. The additional records detailing donors’ preferences show at least nine wanted to remain anonymous.

The Post attempted to reach all the donors whose names appear in this report. Most did not respond or declined to comment. Those who did comment said that there was no connection between their donations and any favorable government actions.

Nvidia, the world’s most valuable public company, became a top contributor to the ballroom in October 2025, nearly three months after it struck a groundbreaking pact with Trump to sell advanced microchips to China despite national security concerns.

CEO Jensen Huang told reporters at the time that the company was contributing to Trump’s ballroom “in a small way” but did not provide a dollar amount. Documents show Nvidia requested that its $25 million donation be kept anonymous.

“As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said in response to questions from The Post. “We were proud to be able to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves all Americans and have said so publicly since the donation was made.”

Major GOP donor Joseph Popolo Jr., Trump’s ambassador to the Netherlands, and his wife contributed $1 million from their family fund to support the ballroom project in late 2025, the records show. Their donation - made two months after Popolo’s confirmation - has not been previously reported.

Trump Cabinet member Kelly Loeffler of the Small Business Administration and her husband Jeff Sprecher, former chairman of the New York Stock Exchange, promised $5 million for the project, the list shows. Brandon Lutnick, chairman of investment bank Cantor Fitzgerald and the son of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, donated stock worth more than $2.5 million, the records show.

Popolo, Loeffler, Sprecher and the Lutnicks did not respond to requests for comment.

More than three-quarters of the money for the ballroom came in commitments of $5 million or more. Among the top donors are some of America’s blue-chip companies, including Amazon, Caterpillar, Comcast, Microsoft and T-Mobile. (Amazon Executive Chairman Jeff Bezos owns The Post.)

Cryptocurrency companies, now under loosened regulations from the Trump administration, and their investors promised more than $18 million. The largest portion came from Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, co-founders of the Gemini crypto exchange, who together donated bitcoin valued at $5,050,018, the records show.

The Winklevoss brothers did not respond to requests for comment.

The ballroom project has also received dozens of small contributions, some as low as $10. The list and additional documents show the source of all but $24,000 of the total donations.

The total fundraising amount falls short of the $400 million Trump has said he intends to raise for the work. The cost of building the new East Wing, which includes the ballroom, office space and an underground military facility, was projected in March to have increased to $600 million, an estimate previously reported by The Post. The White House has used taxpayer dollars to cover some of the construction cost, records show.

The ballroom donations are routed through the Trust for the National Mall, a D.C.-based nonprofit whose mission is to restore and preserve the National Mall and the White House grounds. Nonprofits are not generally required to disclose their donors.

Prospective donors were sent a “pledge agreement form,” a copy of which was obtained by The Post, for giving toward the “Donald J. Trump Ballroom.” The form lists Meredith O’Rourke, the top fundraiser for Trump’s 2024 campaign, as the main contact.

O’Rourke referred questions to the White House.

A 12-page agreement between the government and the Trust requires that the Trust “maintain the anonymity of Project donors to the extent provided by law and not publicly recognize any such donor unless explicitly authorized in writing” by staff in the White House’s Executive Residence unit.

Democratic lawmakers have denounced the fundraising for the ballroom as secretive and potentially transactional. They have demanded that the administration and the Trust provide details about the donors and circumstances of the gifts. Those demands have been rebuffed.

In a statement the Trust said: “In philanthropy, it is not uncommon for donors to request their gifts remain anonymous. The Trust is committed to honoring donors requesting anonymity.”

Pardon for international banker

One of the earliest commitments to donate to the ballroom, from Sept. 23, 2025, came from the daughter of Julio Herrera Velutini, an international banker and dual Venezuelan-Italian citizen.

In 2022, the Justice Department indicted Herrera Velutini, then 50, on bribery charges, accusing him of helping finance the campaign of Puerto Rico’s then-governor in exchange for the removal of a regulator investigating his bank. The former governor and a political consultant were also charged.

Herrera Velutini and his attorney unsuccessfully tried to get the case dismissed, claiming prosecutors were criminalizing lawful political activity.

After Trump’s victory, Herrera’s daughter, Isabela Herrera, made two donations to Trump’s MAGA Inc., a political action committee, totaling $3.5 million, campaign finance records show.

The donations prompted the nonprofit Campaign Legal Center to file a complaint with the Federal Election Commission alleging that Isabela Herrera was serving as a “straw donor” for her father. The organization described her as a self-employed financial consultant in her mid-20s whose only prior political donation was $20 to Pete Buttigieg, a 2020 Democratic presidential candidate.

The organization said it got no response from the FEC, which declined to comment for this story.

In August 2025, Herrera Velutini’s charges were reduced to a misdemeanor as part of a plea agreement.

The following month, Isabela Herrera committed to donating $2.5 million for the ballroom, which has not been previously reported. Records show she paid a first installment of $835,000 on Oct. 14, 2025. Trump pardoned Herrera Velutini in January. Herrera’s second payment was due this month, the records show.

Amid a wider Justice Department retreat from sweeping public corruption investigations, Trump also pardoned the former governor and the political consultant. The White House said the prosecutions had been politically motivated.

After the pardon, an attorney for Herrera Velutini issued a statement saying his client was “profoundly grateful to President Donald J. Trump for bestowing the grace of his benevolent pardon.”

Neither Herrera Velutini nor his daughter responded to requests for comment.

A dropped investigation

Last year, Ergen, the telecommunications executive, found his company EchoStar in the Trump administration’s crosshairs.

Brendan Carr, the chair of the Federal Communications Commission, wrote Ergen in May to inform him that the agency had begun investigating EchoStar. Carr threatened to yank government licenses that were critical to the survival of the business, accusing EchoStar, owner of Dish Network, of not following through on promises it had made to upgrade its cellphone network.

The following month, Ergen met with Trump and Carr behind closed doors to discuss the investigation, according to Bloomberg. The outlet, citing unnamed sources, said the June 11 discussion included a brief exchange about Ergen’s political donations and whether he gave to candidates in both political parties.

The company referenced a June 11 meeting between Ergen and Carr in a regulatory filing and wrote that Trump “subsequently encouraged the parties involved to reach an amicable resolution.”

Ergen negotiated a deal to sell some of the company’s licenses to AT&T in August, subject to approval of the FCC and Justice Department.

Carr dropped the investigation the following month, thanking Ergen for his responses and for information he had provided.

In December, with the sale still pending, Ergen committed $12.5 million to Trump’s ballroom, according to the donation list. Records indicate Ergen requested that the source of the donation remain anonymous. The donation has not been previously reported.

He committed another $12.5 million in February, according to the list.

In May, the FCC and the Justice Department each gave EchoStar approval for the sale.

Through a spokesman, Ergen and EchoStar declined to comment. The FCC and Carr did not respond. DOJ did not provide comment for this story.

The donor list also shows $5 million “pledged” by AT&T, the only line item on the list described that way. Every other amount is listed as “won.”

In a statement to The Post, AT&T spokesperson Megan Ketterer said the company appeared to have been listed in error. “We have no idea what list you are talking about and have no plans to contribute to the Trust for the National Mall,” Ketterer said.

An approval, then a donation

Another top donor was a subsidiary of Rocket, the Detroit-based housing, finance and tech company founded by Daniel Gilbert, owner of the NBA’s Cleveland Cavaliers.

In March 2025, Rocket said that it planned to acquire two competitors: the home search site Redfin and the mortgage site Mr. Cooper. The moves would give Rocket a much larger share of the real estate market.

Federal agencies tasked with protecting against anticompetitive business practices declined to challenge the deals, allowing them to proceed. Five Democratic senators wrote to the Justice Department and Federal Trade Commission in protest.

To acquire Mr. Cooper, Gilbert also needed approval from the Federal Housing Finance Agency.

The FHFA approved the deal on Aug. 26, 2025.

The Rocket subsidiary committed $10 million to the ballroom three weeks later. Records show it requested anonymity.

A Rocket spokesperson said the approvals and donation were not connected.

“Rocket and its related companies have supported the Trust for the National Mall and other nonpartisan organizations in Washington for more than a decade,” said spokesperson Aaron Emerson. “We’re proud to join dozens of companies and individuals in improving our nation’s capital.”

An FTC spokesperson said Rocket received no special treatment, pointing to a lawsuit the agency brought against Redfin for anticompetitive practices days after the donation.

The FHFA and the Justice Department did not provide comment.

Software contracts

One of the country’s leading software providers, Salesforce, has significantly grown its government contracting business during the second Trump administration.

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff has attended exclusive dinners and events with Trump, including a state dinner hosted by King Charles III at Windsor Castle in September 2025 and a business summit in Japan the following month. While there, Trump thanked Benioff for previously putting him on the cover of Time magazine, which Benioff owns.

“Marc has some pretty good suggestions,” Trump said of the CEO.

The following day, Benioff committed $1 million to the ballroom, according to the list. The donation has not previously been reported, and Benioff asked that it remain anonymous.

Salesforce separately made two $1 million commitments to the ballroom, one last Christmas Eve and another Jan. 29 of this year, the list shows. The donations have not been previously reported.

In between, the Army awarded the company a contract worth up to $5.6 billion through 2035, which appears to be the largest public government contract in Salesforce’s history, according to a review of public contracting records. Announcing the contract, the Pentagon said “bids were solicited via the internet with only one received.”

Benioff and Salesforce did not respond to requests for comment.

In a statement, a Pentagon official said: “Outside affiliations, investors, or political connections play absolutely no role in the Department’s funding decisions.”

After this article published, an Army spokesperson said in a statement that contracts are awarded in strict compliance with federal law and are “determined exclusively by validated mission requirements, technical capability, and best value.”

One of Salesforce’s competitors, ServiceNow, also donated to the ballroom.

Last September, the General Services Administration announced what it called a “landmark” agreement with ServiceNow that would make the company’s AI-driven software available to federal agencies at a discount.

“When President Trump says the federal government needs to operate like a best-run business, he means it,” CEO Bill McDermott said as part of the announcement.

The next month, ServiceNow committed $5 million to the ballroom, a donation that has not been previously reported.

The GSA said in a statement that ServiceNow has been a federal contractor for more than a decade, adding that “its charitable or political donations - like those of any company - have no bearing on GSA’s decision to include them in federal buying catalogs.”

ServiceNow said in a statement that negotiations for the deal had been underway for a “considerable period of time.” Its government business is “separate and unconnected to any donations we make to any cause,” it said.

Of the donation, the company said: “Many of our partners and peers were also contributing to the project. We chose to join them.”

Venezuelan oil interests

Nearly $10 million for the ballroom was committed by two Trump political donors who have pursued large investments in Venezuelan oil - a market Trump has gained influence over since the U.S. seizure of President Nicolás Maduro in January.

Billionaire financier Paul Singer committed to donate $5 million through his foundation in October 2025, a month before his hedge fund received court approval to pursue a purchase of Venezuelan oil giant Citgo for $5.9 billion.

The deal will require approval from multiple federal agencies, including the Commerce Department, Energy Department, State Department and Treasury Department. It has stalled amid ongoing negotiations with the South American country’s U.S.-backed administration.

The Oklahoma oil and gas company Continental Resources and its chairman emeritus, billionaire and GOP megadonor Harold Hamm, both promised donations to the ballroom in October 2025 totaling just under $5 million.

This year, in response to the Trump administration’s call for energy companies to invest in the Venezuelan oil industry, Continental struck a tentative agreement with the country’s state-run oil company to develop 126,000 acres of untapped oil fields.

Singer declined to comment. Neither Hamm nor Continental responded.

Unlisted

Two companies and one individual the White House has publicly named as donors do not appear on the list obtained by The Post.

The companies are Hard Rock International, the hospitality chain owned by the Seminole Tribe of Florida, and Tether America, a cryptocurrency firm. The individual is Paolo Tiramani, a modular homes company executive who told the Times of London that he had donated $10 million in stock.

None of the three answered The Post’s questions or explained why they are not recorded as having contributed to the ballroom fundraising campaign. Neither did the Trust for the National Mall or the White House.

Kevin Crowe, Samantha Schmidt, Dan Lamothe and Alex Horton contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump admin. sues California over alleged noncitizens on state's voter rolls
item.description:
By Andrew Goudsward and Luc Cohen

WASHINGTON, Oct 15 (Reuters) - The US Justice Department sued California on Thursday, asking a federal judge to block the state from counting mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections from more than 20,000 voters the Trump administration alleges are ‌likely noncitizens.

The lawsuit marks the latest effort by President Donald Trump's administration to boost the federal government's role in elections ahead of the ‌midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress.

The US Constitution assigns the responsibility of administering elections to individual states, though the federal government ​has some oversight role.

Trump has repeatedly claimed that voting by noncitizens - which is illegal - is widespread, despite multiple studies showing it is rare. A Reuters investigation published in July found that just 129 people had been prosecuted for noncitizen voting since the statute criminalizing it passed in 1996. The Justice Department has ramped up such prosecutions in recent months.

In the lawsuit filed in federal court in Los Angeles, the Justice Department sought a court order preventing California from "tabulating in federal elections vote-by-mail ballots received" ‌from more than 20,000 voters until their immigration status is ⁠verified.

Reuters previously reported that the department sent California a letter giving it a 48-hour deadline on Tuesday to review the list of alleged noncitizen voters. The list was provided on a thumb drive.

CALIFORNIA SAYS DOJ SEEKS CHAOS

The lawsuit marks an escalation ⁠in the federal government's pressure on state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting.

The Justice Department has warned election officials in all 50 states that they could face criminal prosecution if they knowingly allowed noncitizens to remain on their voter rolls or cast ballots. It has sued 30 states and Washington DC for refusing to provide complete voter rolls including voters' ​sensitive ​personal data, but has lost 26 of those cases so far without winning one.

In Thursday's ​lawsuit against California, the Justice Department said the Department of Homeland ‌Security had identified the 20,000 alleged noncitizens by comparing voter rolls to its own internal databases.

Voting rights activists have expressed concern that many citizens who are naturalized could be wrongly flagged as noncitizens due to outdated DHS data.

California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan, who were named as defendants in the lawsuit, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In a statement on Wednesday about the letter, Weber said California's safeguards against noncitizen voting were robust.

"The USDOJ's relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in ‌our elections," Weber said.

NONCITIZENS HAVE BEEN REGISTERED THROUGH ERRORS

Though states may have added more than ​30,000 noncitizens to their voter rolls since 2000 due to software glitches and clerical errors, Reuters ​found in September, it was unclear how many had cast a ballot. ​Experts said the numbers were too small relative to the country’s 170 million registered voters to affect elections.

Rick Hasen, a law ‌professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, and an expert ​on election law, said the DOJ’s request ​would potentially cause California to violate a federal law barring states from conducting mass purges of voter rolls within 90 days of an election.

The Trump administration has argued in another case that such restrictions should not apply to removal of noncitizens because they were not legally authorized to ​register in the first place.

Hasen said the DOJ lawsuit would ‌likely face legal hurdles.

“The federal government doesn’t have any business directly telling states what ballots they can or cannot send out or ​not count,” he said. “I just don’t see the federal authority to do that over a state.”

(Reporting by Andrew Goudsward in Washington and Luc ​Cohen in New York; Editing by Michelle Nichols, Matthew Lewis and David Gregorio)

This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/doj-sues-california-block-votes-171601356.html

item.description:
美股周四（10月15日）震荡收高，道指上涨556点，涨幅1.08%，标普500指数上涨0.33%，纳指从盘中下跌超过1.4%逆转收涨0.08%。尽管美国9月生产者价格同比上涨6.3%，创2022年以来最大涨幅，但市场对AI企业债务风险和资本开支可持续性的担忧压过通胀冲击，避险资金推动美债上涨，10年期国债收益率降至5.086%。CoreWeave信用风险指标进入困境区间，凸显AI投资正从估值调整转向融资能力和现金流的考验。资金明显撤离科技股，转向医疗保健、金融和消费板块。分析师认为，未来市场将更加重视AI企业的债务负担、资本使用效率及盈利能力。
